identity.name: The Economist
identity.description: A weekly news and current-affairs magazine offering data-rich analysis of economics, geopolitics, business, technology and culture from a classical-liberal perspective.

ownership.ownershipNotes: The Economist Group is independently owned through a dual-class structure with significant historic shareholders including the Cadbury, Rothschild, Schroder and Agnelli families. Editorial independence is constitutionally protected.

editorialOrientation.evidence: The group's constitution and editorial charter protect independence; the magazine takes explicit classical-liberal positions while distinguishing analysis from reporting.
editorialOrientation.source: Ownership and self-description via Official about page; secondary references; feed-level sample

politicalLeaning.evidence: MBFC rates The Economist Least Biased with High factual reporting; its editorial line is classical-liberal and pro-market rather than partisan-centrist.

economicPerspective.evidence: Consistent advocacy for free markets, open trade, fiscal discipline and liberal immigration, tempered by support for some state capacity and climate policy.

internationalAlignment.evidence: Frames world affairs through liberal internationalism, open markets and alliance politics, with a distinctly Anglo-American analytical audience.
internationalAlignment.source: Ownership, editorial positioning and regional coverage sample

reliability.evidence: MBFC rates factual reporting High and credibility High; bylined analysis, corrections and transparent data sourcing support reliability, though analysis is interpretive.

externalRatings.notes: MBFC: Least Biased; factual reporting High; credibility High (retrieved 2026-10-25).

intelligence.knownPerspective: Analytical, data-driven classical liberalism. Explains events through incentives, institutions, markets and long-run trends, often with a clear editorial judgment about policy.
knownWeaknesses: Editorial voice can blur analysis and opinion

selectionRationale: Adds high-quality explanatory and data journalism that helps the system interpret economics and geopolitics rather than merely record events.

feeds.validationNote: 300 items; valid RSS; headline/summary feed rather than full articles.

research.researchNotes: Ownership and editorial independence confirmed through The Economist Group and Wikipedia. Feed is valid but contains summary-level items; article sampling was not performed. Research is feed-level only; full article sampling and peer review remain outstanding.
